stem: A 3-year-old boy is brought to the office because he has difficulty keeping up with other children his age.  He also needs to use his hands to push against his legs when rising from the floor.  Physical examination shows enlarged calves.  This patient's condition is most likely associated with which of the following?​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌​​​​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌

explanation:
Duchenne muscular dystrophy

Pathophysiology

  • Mutation in dystrophin gene on X chromosome
  • Absent dystrophin in muscle cytoskeleton
  • Muscle atrophy → muscle replacement with connective tissue/fat

Clinical findings

  • Proximal muscle weakness (boys age 2-3)
    • Delayed motor milestones
    • Gowers sign, calf pseudohypertrophy
  • Scoliosis, lumbar lordosis
  • Dilated cardiomyopathy & restrictive lung disease

Evaluation

  • ↑ Serum creatine kinase
  • Genetic analysis (diagnostic)

This patient's calf enlargement and Gowers sign, in which a child uses the hands to push against the legs when rising to compensate for proximal muscle weakness, are characteristic of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD).  DMD usually results from out-of-frame deletions or other mutations in the dystrophin gene that prevent production of functional dystrophin.

Dystrophin provides mechanical stability to the sarcolemma of skeletal and cardiac muscle fibers.  It links intracellular actin to a membrane protein complex connected to the extracellular matrix, stabilizing the muscle cell membrane during contraction.  Without dystrophin, contraction causes membrane injury and increased calcium entry into muscle cells.  Calcium overload activates proteases and other pathways that promote muscle fiber necrosis, resulting in progressive weakness.

The proximal lower extremities are affected early, causing gait abnormalities and difficulty rising from the floor.  Repeated muscle fiber degeneration and regeneration eventually lead to replacement by fat and connective tissue, causing calf pseudohypertrophy despite muscle weakness.

(Choice A)  Endomysial inflammatory infiltration is characteristic of polymyositis, which causes proximal muscle weakness but typically does not cause calf pseudohypertrophy.  In contrast, DMD is characterized by muscle fiber degeneration and progressive fibrofatty replacement.

(Choice B)  Guillain-Barré syndrome typically involves endoneurial inflammation and demyelination, causing acute ascending weakness and decreased reflexes.  Chronic proximal weakness and calf pseudohypertrophy are not characteristic.

(Choice C)  Muscle ion channel disorders include hyperkalemic and hypokalemic periodic paralysis, which cause episodic, painless muscle weakness.  This child's persistent weakness and calf pseudohypertrophy favor DMD.

(Choice D)  Demyelinating forms of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease result from genetic abnormalities affecting peripheral myelin proteins.  Patients typically have distal muscle weakness, sensory loss, decreased reflexes, and calf muscle atrophy.

(Choice F)  Sarcomere protein mutations cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, some forms of familial dilated cardiomyopathy, and certain inherited skeletal myopathies.  Dystrophin instead links the cytoskeleton to the sarcolemma; it is not a component of the sarcomere.

Educational objective:Duchenne muscular dystrophy is an X-linked recessive disorder that typically presents in young boys with proximal muscle weakness, Gowers sign, and calf pseudohypertrophy.  Dystrophin links the intracellular actin cytoskeleton to a transmembrane protein complex connected to the extracellular matrix.  Loss of functional dystrophin causes membrane instability, muscle fiber necrosis, and progressive fibrofatty replacement.​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌​​​​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​‌​​‌​​‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​​​​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌
